next_steps: Redwood to share per-route latency + cost CSV and the small benchmark traces (Omar) — due 2025-12-12
Customer to run a 1k-sample synthetic regression against v2-quant and report hallucination rate (Ava) — due 2025-12-11
Schedule a canary rollout window for v2 on dev traffic next Tuesday (Maya to coordinate) — meeting invite by 2025-12-10
Security doc pack (SOC2 summary, KMS notes) sent to legal — Redwood to attach in follow-up email
action_items: Omar: produce per-route latency/cost delta spreadsheet comparing v1.2, v2, and v2-quant by 2025-12-12
Ava: run 1000-record synthetic eval with v2-quant and measure answer-quality/regression by 2025-12-11
Maya: schedule canary rollout & share the rollout runbook and playbook by 2025-12-10

meeting_header: Recorded: 2025-12-09 15:00 PST | Duration: 48m | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Omar Basri (Redwood SE), Ava Patel (Cobalt ML), Leo Ramos (Cobalt Platform), Nora Kim (Cobalt CTO)
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on narrowing candidate models for the pilot, validating v2-quant performance, and agreeing a safe rollback/fallback plan. Redwood will deliver latency/cost deltas and rollout runbook; customer will execute synthetic evaluations and confirm infra windows.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:07] Ava Patel (Cobalt): Ava here.
[00:09] Leo Ramos (Cobalt): Leo on the call.
[00:11] Nora Kim (Cobalt): Nora, hi.
[00:13] Omar Basri (Redwood SE): Omar here. Cool.
[00:18] Maya: Ok quick agenda: 1) review last week's benchmark results, 2) decide which model variants we pilot next week, 3) agree rollback/fallback playbook. Any additions?
[00:28] Nora: No, that's good. High level we want to avoid user-facing regressions — that's the priority.
[00:34] Ava: Also want to make sure we don't blow the latency SLO in the feed pipeline.
[00:38] Maya: Great. Omar, can you walk us through the per-route deltas you ran?
[00:43] Omar: Sure. I posted the raw traces in the shared drive, link in the chat. Quick summary: v2 (the larger open model) gives about a 7-9% gain in quality on our eval set but is ~30% slower p95 compared to v1.2 on the same GPU. v2-quant (int8-ish quantized variant) recovers most latency — p95 only ~10% higher than v1.2 — but we saw a small bump in the hallucination metric on a sensitive prompt subset.
[01:15] Ava: When you say hallucination bump, what's the magnitude?
[01:18] Omar: On that subset the false-assertion rate moved from 1.6% to 2.7% — so absolute +1.1 points. It's noisy but consistent across three runs.
[01:29] Leo: Is that from quantization artifacts or model differences?
[01:32] Omar: Good question. We suspect quant noise plus slightly different tokenization edge cases. We didn't change prompts; these are raw model outputs.
[01:39] Nora: Can we mitigate with prompt engineering or post-filtering?
[01:42] Omar: Yes, two options: 1) small prompt tweaks and reranking which recovers most errors but adds latency; 2) hybrid path — route sensitive prompts to v1.2 and bulk traffic to v2-quant. That's where model-pinning and routing policies come in.
[01:58] Maya: Ava, do you have per-route traffic breakdowns to gauge how much would hit the sensitive set?
[02:03] Ava: Roughly 12% of requests are in the sensitive class by current heuristics. So routing to v1.2 for that slice is feasible.
[02:10] Leo: On infra, we need to understand how session KV cache behaves across pinned versions — if users are pinned to v1.2 and then we switch, do we lose context?
[02:20] Omar: The runtime manages KV per model variant. If you pin a session to a model id, the KV is compatible only within that model family. We can enable cross-variant migrations but that's a live migration task; recommended approach is soft-fallbacks not hard switch mid-session.
[02:36] Nora: So the safe strategy would be route by request-type, not by session?
[02:40] Omar: Exactly, or continue sessions on the same model until natural session end. For long-lived sessions we recommend sticky pinning until user disconnect.
[02:48] Maya: Let's walk through the rollback playbook. Omar?
[02:51] Omar: Playbook draft: 1) Canary: deploy v2-quant to 5% of traffic for non-sensitive routes for 24h, monitor p95 latency and hallucination metric; 2) If hallucination delta > 1.5 points or error rate increases, cut to 0% and route back to v1.2; 3) If latency exceeds SLO (we agreed SLO 600ms p95 for these routes), throttle batch sizes or fall back to smaller variant; 4) Postmortem + RCA before reattempt. Runbook includes step-by-step commands, dashboards and the rollback curl commands.
[03:28] Leo: That sounds good. On the canary window — can we control traffic split on the Redwood console or will we do header flagging?
[03:36] Omar: Both. The console supports per-route percentage routing, and you can also set header-based overrides if you want to target specific cohorts.
[03:43] Ava: One practical question: if we pin a model version in our code, how do we pin to both workspace and the actual model artifact? We had a bug before where the config pointed to a logical name and the backend rolled forward.
[03:55] Maya: Good catch. Our recommended pattern: pin to immutable model-id (the sha-like artifact id) and in Redwood Console lock the route to that model-id. We'll also hand you a small CI check that fails deploys if the model-id in code doesn't match the pinned route.
[04:09] Nora: Can you provide the sample CI snippet?
[04:11] Maya: Yes, will include in the follow-up email.
[04:14] Ava: About metrics — can Redwood provide traced token-level latency so we can see where batching adds overhead?
[04:20] Omar: Yep. We can export token-level histograms and a sample trace bundle. Those are the files I put in the drive; I'll add per-route breakdowns as a CSV.
[04:29] Maya: For security/compliance, Leo wanted the SOC2 summary and KMS integration details. Omar, you said there was an updated pack?
[04:37] Omar: Yes, I have a short SOC2 one-pager and KMS notes. We'll attach to the follow-up and cc legal. Note: in Private we support customer-managed keys via HSM; in Dedicated we have KMS integration.
[04:51] Leo: We need to confirm egress costs for the production window — the finance team asked.
[04:54] Maya: We'll include an estimated cost delta in the per-route spreadsheet.
[04:58] Ava: Quick note on hallucination: some of the false assertions are low-confidence factual dates that our downstream QA can filter. So a small bump might be acceptable if cost and latency are better. But we need the exact number so product can decide.
[05:13] Nora: Also want an explicit SLA on the canary timebox — we don't want a canary that lingers if something noisy shows up.
[05:19] Omar: Runbook includes auto-rolloff condition and an alerting threshold to auto-cut the canary.
[05:24] Maya: Let's hash out the routing options — simplest approach is route sensitive class to v1.2, everything else to v2-quant, with a 5% canary on new non-sensitive routes. Any objections?
[05:37] Ava: Sounds good. We should also consider a staged pin: start with dev traffic, then staging, then prod baseline.
[05:43] Omar: We can do that with tagged environments. The Console lets you map workspaces to environment tags, and you can script deployments.
[05:50] Leo: Regarding rollback speed — how quickly can we scale back from 5% to 0%?
[05:54] Omar: Instantly — it's a config flip. If you do it via API or Console it takes seconds, but of course in-flight requests will finish.
[06:00] Maya: Ava, any preliminary results from your synth runs this week?
[06:03] Ava: I ran a 200-sample run against v2 and v2-quant; quality delta looked ok but with the small hallucination bump Omar mentioned. I need to run a larger 1k set to be confident.
[06:14] Nora: Is there an option to add a light-weight reranker that costs a few ms but reduces hallucinations?
[06:19] Omar: Yes, adding a small reranker or verification step is common. Redwood supports a two-step pipeline where you call the model then hit a deterministic verifier (or small classification model) — it adds latency but it can be sub-50ms if optimized.
[06:31] Leo: What's the recommended quant level? Int8 is what you tested?
[06:35] Omar: We tested an 8-bit quant (v2-quant) and also tried 4-bit in an internal run; 4-bit saved more cost but introduced more noise. 8-bit is usually a good trade-off for this workload.
[06:46] Ava: For the session pinning questions — if we do route-by-request-type, how do we ensure analytics and logs tie back across models for a single user?
[06:54] Omar: The platform emits a unified request id and user id; you can correlate logs regardless of which model served the request. We also emit model_id in traces so you can filter.
[07:02] Maya: Let's talk about rollout timeline. Proposed: Monday dev canary, Tuesday staging canary, Wednesday prod 5% for 24h, contingent on metrics. Does that timeline work?
[07:12] Nora: Tight but possible. We need the benchmark CSV by Friday to sign off.
[07:17] Maya: Omar can you commit to that?
[07:19] Omar: Yes, I'll produce the per-route CSV and attach traces by Friday 12/12.
[07:25] Ava: Also will need the prompt CI snippet.
[07:28] Maya: Will include.
[07:29] Leo: On the dedicated vs hosted question — we discussed earlier about data residency. We still intend to evaluate a Private deployment for UK customers, but for this pilot we'll use Redwood Dedicated in us-west.
[07:41] Nora: Agreed. For now keep test data anonymized but production plan includes Private.
[07:47] Omar: Noted — Private has the same API surface but different control plane access. We'll add a short note in the follow-up.
[07:55] Maya: Any blockers from the customer side?
[07:57] Ava: None besides running the larger synth and confirming infra window.
[08:01] Leo: I'll confirm the peering window with infra by Friday.
[08:04] Nora: Legal will want the SOC2 notes; please include those.
[08:08] Maya: We'll attach those.
[08:10] Omar: One more technical note: if you want to do automatic fallback for a particular route, you can set a latency threshold plus error rate and Redwood will automatically route to the fallback model. It's configurable per-route.
[08:22] Ava: That would be useful for our bursty endpoints.
[08:25] Maya: Quick recap before we end: Redwood delivers per-route CSV + traces (Omar), SOC2 + KMS one-pagers (Omar/Maya), CI model-id check and runbook (Maya), Customer runs 1k synthetic eval (Ava), Leo confirms infra peering window (Leo). Canary plan with 5% non-sensitive rollout then expand if green.
[08:45] Nora: Thanks, that's clear.
[08:48] Maya: We'll send notes and the invite for the canary schedule. Thanks everyone.
[08:53] Ava: Thanks.
[08:54] Leo: Thanks all.
[08:56] (call ends)
